memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: One day the older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man around here to give us children - as is the custom all over the earth. Let's get our father to drink wine and then sleep with him and preserve our family line through him." - Gen 19:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a dark and shameful episode, and Scripture records it without any approval. Lot's daughters, having grown up in Sodom, devise a plan to get their father drunk and commit incest with him. It is a grievous sin, and the Bible tells it plainly as a warning, not a model. We should read it soberly, seeing the terrible fruit of a life shaped by a corrupt culture.

Notice where this comes from. These young women had been raised in Sodom, soaked in its values, formed by its disregard for God's ways. When they finally left, Sodom did not leave them. The corruption they grew up in surfaced in their own choices. What we absorb from our environment shapes us, and it shapes our children even more.

This is the sobering legacy of Lot's compromise. Years earlier he "pitched his tents toward Sodom" for its prosperity - and now the moral rot of that city bears bitter fruit in his own family. Our choices about where and how we live ripple down to those who come after us, often in ways we never intended.

Let this drive us to sober reflection rather than mere condemnation. We are all shaped by our surroundings, and we all need God to break the patterns of sin passed down to us. The good news is that no legacy of corruption is beyond God's redemption. Christ came precisely to break the power of inherited sin and make all things new (2 Cor 5:17).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How has your environment shaped you and those you love?
- Do you trust God to break sinful patterns handed down through generations?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, this dark episode sobers me about how deeply our surroundings shape us and our children. Break in me any sinful patterns handed down to me, and make me a fresh beginning of grace through Christ.
Amen.
